description: Each year, team Starflock attempts to uncover trends and connections between different data sets, including data sets from different organizations.  While NASA's Earth data holds immense value in its singularity, integrating it with datasets from USDA, USGS, NOAA, NIH, and other sources can magnify scientific findings.
summary: Different Rates of Climate Change: Differences between the layers of Earth’s atmosphere could impact earth systems differently.  Altitudes is a dashboard developed to better understand these trends.
details:
Layers of the Atmosphere

Exosphere: Atmospheric escape, space interactions.

Thermosphere: Solar radiation, satellites, GPS.

Mesosphere: Meteor protection, atmospheric circulation.

Stratosphere: UV protection, climate, health.

Troposphere: Weather, agriculture, air quality, human health.

AIRS/Aqua

The Atmospheric Infrared Sounder (AIRS) aboard NASA’s Aqua satellite measures atmospheric properties using infrared spectroscopy. Its Support Product provides high-resolution vertical profiles (100 pressure levels) of temperature, humidity, and trace gases. AIRS collects 240 six-minute granules daily, with an approximately 16-day orbital repeat cycle.

Platform: Aqua

Instrument: AIRS (Atmospheric Infrared Sounder)

Project: Aqua

Location: Global

Spatial Extent: 90°N to 90°S, 180°E to 180°W

Spatial Resolution: 50 km × 50 km

Coordinate System: Cartesian

Granule Spatial Representation: Cartesian

Temporal Extent: August 30, 2002 – Present

Data Partner: NASA Goddard Earth Sciences Data and Information Services Center (GES DISC)

Concept ID: C1243477382-GES_DISC

Data State: Active

Number of Files/Granules: 2,087,707

Processing Level: Level 2

Published: November 29, 2019

Keywords: Air Temperature, Carbon Monoxide, Cloud Fraction, Cloud Height, Cloud Top Pressure, Cloud Top Temperature, Cloud Vertical Distribution, Emissivity, Geopotential Height, Methane, Outgoing Longwave Radiation, Atmospheric Ozone, Total Precipitable Water, Sea Surface Temperature, Surface Pressure, Skin Temperature, Surface Temperature, Sulfur Dioxide, Tropopause, Tropospheric Ozone, Upper Air Temperature, Water Vapor Profiles, Cloud Liquid Water/Ice, Cloud Droplet Concentration/Size, Cloud Optical Depth/Thickness, Cloud Types, Precipitation Rate

Project Pipeline

1) Download Data: Download HDF4 files from the NASA Earth Data Search platform: AIRS/Aqua L2 Support Retrieval (AIRS-only) V006 (AIRS2SUP) from 2003-2026; filtered for one day each month, stratified by day/night, and bounded by (23.62486,-124.12358 SW, 49.21384,-66.32728 NE) ROI.

2) Extract/Convert Data: Convert HDF4 files to Parquet format using an R script for downstream analyses.

3) Analyze Data: Analyze Parquet data to calculate changes in atmospheric temperature and composition, comparing same-month data between 2003 and 2026, for each pressure level (100 levels total), which is correlated with altitude.

4) Data Visualization: Create an interactive dashboard with plots and maps to display the changes in atmospheric temperature and composition, openly accessible to the general public.  

Example Findings

1) Temperature changes greatest in troposphere and upper stratosphere

2) Temperature changes greatest at night vs day

3) Methane changes in mesosphere greatest in winter months

4) Ozone decreased most significantly in the stratosphere in late summer
